previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for aspirin desensitization to enable further cardiac evaluation after a prior NSTEMI. She had a history of aspirin allergy with hives and shortness of breath, requiring inpatient desensitization. Her renal function was impaired (creatinine 1.9) due to prior contrast-induced nephropathy and hypertensive injury, delaying cardiac catheterization. Prehydration and Mucomyst were given for renal protection. Aspirin desensitization was completed successfully without reaction. Cardiac catheterization revealed stable two-vessel coronary disease not amenable to stenting, and cardiothoracic surgery is evaluating her for bypass pending optimization of comorbidities. Blood pressure was controlled with hydralazine and amlodipine; labetolol was restarted post-desensitization. Lisinopril and lasix were held due to renal concerns. She was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with strict instructions to continue daily aspirin to avoid repeat desensitization, monitor weight, and follow up with cardiology and primary care.

follow her renal insufficiency.

her glucose were to become frequently elevated above 140 as her 
intake improves, sliding scale coverage would be indicated.

about 4 kilograms above her preoperative weight, but diuretics 
have been on hold due to her renal dysfunction.  She has had 
good urine output and weight decreases without treatment.There 
remains some peripheral edema that should resolve with increased 
activity and autodiuresis.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female status post CABG.

STUDY:  Portable supine AP chest radiograph.

COMPARISON:  Preoperative film from ___.

FINDINGS:  The endotracheal tube is 1 cm above the carina.  Right-sided Swan
catheter coils within the left main pulmonary artery.  An endogastric tube
courses inferiorly with its side port just below the GE junction.  Chest tubes
and mediastinal drains project over the mediastinum.

The patient is rotated toward the right.  Midline sternotomy wires are intact.
The heart and mediastinal contours are consistent with post-CABG findings. 
The hila are unremarkable.  The lungs are clear of masses or consolidation;
retrocardiac atelectasis is seen, a common post-operative finding.  There is
no large pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:
1.  ET tube 1 cm above the carina, would recommend pulling back 3 or 4 cm.
2.  Right-sided Swan-Ganz catheter coiling within the left main pulmonary
artery.  Recommend pulling back 6-8 cm.
3.  No large pleural effusion or pneumothorax.
These findings were communicated to ___ at 17:00 on ___.

SINGLE AP PORTABLE VIEW OF THE CHEST

REASON FOR EXAM:  Tachypnea.

Comparison is made with prior study performed 6 hours earlier.

Mild pulmonary edema is new.  There is no evident pneumothorax. 
Cardiomediastinal contours are unchanged.  ET tube is in the standard
position.  Swan-Ganz catheter tip is in the left pulmonary artery.  Chest
tubes remain in place.  Sternal wires are aligned.

PORTABLE CHEST, ___

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Interval removal of Swan-Ganz catheter and placement of right
internal jugular central venous catheter with tip near the junction of the
superior vena cava and right atrium.  Precise location is somewhat difficult
to assess due to marked patient rotation and low lung volumes.  Other
indwelling devices are unchanged in position.  Cardiomediastinal contours are
similar to the prior study allowing for positional differences between the
exams.  Worsening atelectasis in the left lower lobe as well as an increasing
small left pleural effusion.  Focal atelectasis is also present adjacent to
the right-sided chest tube.

HISTORY:  ___ female status post CABG x3.

STUDY:  AP semi-upright portable chest radiograph.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  There has been interval removal of the endotracheal tube,
endogastric tube, chest tubes and mediastinal drain.  The right-sided central
line tip is in the upper right atrium.  The cardiomediastinal contours appear
prominent.  Retrocardiac atelectasis persists.  The lung volumes overall are
low.  Linear atelectasis is also seen in the right lung base, and there is
loss of volume of the right middle lobe.  There are small bilateral pleural
effusions.  There is no large pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Interval removal of endotracheal, endogastric, chest tubes, and
mediastinal drain.
2.  Mild increase in cardiomediastinal prominence - if concern for tampondae,
would correlate with echocardiography.
3.  Partial loss of volume of the right middle lobe; persistent retrocardiac
atelectasis.
4.  No large pneumothorax.

2.  Slowly progressive enlargement of cardiac silhouette could represent

FINDINGS:  Single portable supine abdominal radiograph is extremely

dilated bowel loop is evident to suggest obstruction.  

IMPRESSION:  Extremely limited exam.  Likely no evidence of obstruction.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Followup on the patient seven days after CABG.

PA and lateral upright chest radiographs were compared to ___.

The right internal jugular line tip is at the level of cavoatrial junction. 
Cardiomediastinal silhouette is unchanged including cardiomegaly. 
Post-sternotomy wires are unchanged.  There is minimal upper zone
redistribution of vasculature and minimal interstitial engorgement but no
overt pulmonary edema.  Bibasilar retrocardiac opacities are most likely

be excluded but no appreciable pleural effusion is seen.
